structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the metacarpus length-to-breadth ratio (slenderness) of sheep is about 1.5 times, and of giraffe about 3 times, that of the ox, while the breadth proportions among widths (proximal, midshaft, distal) are nearly the same in all three, so one longitudinal stretch relates the bones.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using species-mean metacarpus data, with slenderness S = full length (MC1) / midshaft mediolateral width (MC3): S_sheep/S_ox between 1.2 and 1.8 (1.5 ±20%) AND S_giraffe/S_ox between 2.4 and 3.6 (3 ±20%), AND the one-axis condition holds: the ratios of distal width (MC4) to midshaft width and proximal width (MC5) to midshaft width for sheep and giraffe each lie within ±15% of the ox values. All conditions must be met.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Claim refuted if S_sheep/S_ox is below 1.2 or above 1.8, OR S_giraffe/S_ox is below 2.4 or above 3.6, OR any width-proportion ratio (MC4/MC3, MC5/MC3) of sheep or giraffe differs from ox by more than 25%, which would mean the bones differ in more than length versus breadth.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'cannon-bone' is the fused metacarpal III+IV (metacarpus) of ruminants; the dataset records it as metacarpus measurements. 'Elongated along the vertical axis in the relation of 3/2' means the sheep length/breadth ratio is 1.5 times the ox's, which equals a breadth at equal length of 2/3 of the ox's. The giraffe's breadth of 1/3 means a ratio of 3. Breadth is taken as midshaft mediolateral width, and the shape check uses proximal and distal widths. Modern reinterpretation: the test uses species means rather than Thompson's single drawn specimens, with Bos taurus (or the available Bos species), Ovis aries (or the available Ovis species) and Giraffa camelopardalis as the taxa; if a taxon is missing from the file the test cannot be run. The one-axis check uses width ratios rather than Procrustes shape analysis. Variable names MC1 to MC5 follow the supplementary documentation of the associated paper and must be checked against the README and file headers.

dataset.name: Predicting body mass in Ruminantia using postcranial measurements
dataset.why_it_fits: The dataset covers 101 extant ruminant species (including bovids and giraffids) and has body_mass_data.csv with species means of 56 postcranial linear measurements, plus raw per-individual measurements in raw_postcranial_measurements.xlsx. Per the associated paper's supplement, these include metacarpus full length, midshaft width, and proximal and distal widths, which are the quantities needed for slenderness and width-proportion ratios. The landing page does not list individual species or column names, so the presence of Bos, Ovis and Giraffa and of the metacarpus columns is unconfirmed until the files are opened.
